evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes sponsor creation/management capabilities (e.g., becoming a sponsor and sponsor profile personalization), so viewing sponsors is not missing a necessary complementary capability.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes user registration and profile update, which provides the complementary capability needed for profiles to exist and be maintained.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website
evaluations.rationale: Bulk-emailing trainers presumes the system can identify who the trainers are (trainer role/association to trainings) and have their contact info; the backlog lacks an explicit story to manage trainer accounts/roles or maintain trainer contact details.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes venue creation/maintenance and venue detail viewing, which can supply the underlying location data needed for maps.

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself
evaluations.rationale: Editing a training node implies training nodes exist and can be created/initially authored; the backlog has multiple stories to view trainings but no explicit story to create/submit/manage training offerings (call for trainings is promotional only).

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: This constraint presumes a training registration capability exists; the backlog includes waitlist and cancellation workflow but lacks an explicit story to register for a training.

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee
evaluations.rationale: Tracking registration status presumes a training registration and status lifecycle exists (registered/attended/refunded/no show); backlog lacks an explicit training registration story and explicit mechanisms to mark attendance/no-show for trainings.

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: Waitlisting is complementary to a primary training registration/enrollment capability and capacity management; backlog lacks an explicit story to register for a training.

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Acceptance of cancellation terms is part of a registration/cancellation workflow; backlog lacks an explicit training registration story to which this checkbox would attach.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: A cancellation deadline requires an implemented registration/cancellation workflow; backlog does not include an explicit training registration story (and cancellation flow is only referenced indirectly).

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: Adding items to 'my schedule' implies a personal schedule feature with persistence and retrieval; backlog includes viewing the overall schedule but lacks explicit creation/management of a personal schedule list.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Seeing signed-up trainings presumes a training signup/registration capability exists; backlog lacks an explicit story to register for a training.

evaluations.evidence: view ... attached to their training node that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: Trainer viewing attendee info presumes attendees can register for trainings and that attendee lists exist; backlog lacks an explicit training registration story.

evaluations.evidence: admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session
evaluations.rationale: Filtering trainee info by training session presumes training session enrollment data exists; backlog lacks an explicit training registration story.

evaluations.evidence: dedicated page for each class ... link to register for class
evaluations.rationale: The story requires a 'link to register for class', implying a training registration capability; backlog does not include an explicit story to register for a training.

evaluations.evidence: register now link
evaluations.rationale: A 'register now' link implies training registration exists; backlog lacks an explicit training registration story.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page ... promote call for trainings
evaluations.rationale: A call for trainings implies trainers can submit/create training offerings; backlog lacks an explicit story for creating/submitting training offerings (only editing/viewing is present).

evaluations.evidence: link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes training landing/listing pages, so the linked destination capability exists.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: This requires the site to store and publish coding lounge location/hours; backlog has venue management generally but no story to create/maintain 'coding lounge' hours/info as content.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refunding presumes sponsorship payments are processed via Stripe; backlog includes paying for sponsorships but does not explicitly establish Stripe payment processing for sponsorships (only referenced here).

evaluations.evidence: link ... to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Becoming a sponsor via payment implies a complete purchase/checkout flow; backlog has payment entry/charge stories but lacks an explicit end-to-end 'complete sponsorship purchase' confirmation/role assignment outcome beyond fragments.

evaluations.evidence: See a list of attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Listing attendees by company requires capturing attendee-to-company affiliation; backlog lacks a story to collect/maintain company association on user profiles or sponsorship linkage.

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes payment page and card charging for sponsorships, which are complementary capabilities for paying.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing venue details, providing the complementary read capability for created venues.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes venue creation/maintenance, so venue details can exist to be viewed.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of the sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Requires (1) sponsor-attendee association and (2) attendee-to-session association; backlog lacks explicit stories to link attendees to sponsors/companies and to track which sessions an attendee is associated with (attendance/registration).

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page ... third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes entering payment information and charging the card, which complements having a payment page.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing sponsor-sponsored items, providing the complementary read capability for these assignments.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes assigning sponsors to events/trainings/summits, enabling this view.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes payment page/step in registration, which complements entering payment info and charging.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Linking attendees to a sponsorship page requires a mechanism to associate specific user accounts with a sponsor/company; backlog lacks an explicit story to create/manage these attendee-to-sponsor/company relationships.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes user registration and viewing profiles, which complements profile updating.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup implies a subscription management capability (store subscriber, manage opt-in/out, send list integration); backlog lacks complementary stories for managing/sending newsletters or integrating with an email service.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creating blog posts and reading the blog, so tagging is a complementary enhancement rather than exposing a missing core capability.

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes reading the blog, providing the complementary consumption capability for created posts.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creating blog posts, so there is a complementary capability to produce content to read.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit
evaluations.rationale: Sponsoring a summit implies a sponsorship purchase/commitment flow and linking sponsorship to a summit; backlog has sponsor assignment to summits but lacks an explicit story for sponsors to complete a summit sponsorship transaction/commitment.

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing seats left, viewing summit details, and coordinators viewing attendee lists, which together support summit registration being meaningful and actionable.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes venue creation/maintenance and viewing venue details, which can provide the underlying location information needed for directions.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit registration, which is the complementary capability needed for a user to have signups to view.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit registration, which provides the attendee signup data needed for this list.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes anonymous users viewing summit details and lists, which complements summit coordinators listing summit information.

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing sponsors for a summit implies sponsors can be associated with a summit; backlog has admin assignment of sponsors to summits but lacks a complementary story for summit coordinators (non-admin) to manage/curate that sponsor list or for sponsors to commit to summit sponsorship in a way that populates it.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: An agenda typically consists of agenda items/sessions; backlog lacks a complementary story to create/manage summit agenda items (beyond generic session submission for the conference).

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit registration, which is the complementary capability needed for seats remaining to change based on signups.

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits ... register for the event
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit registration and summit info listing, so the detail page can be supported by complementary capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit coordinators listing summit information, which provides the complementary capability for summits to exist and be listed.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes stories to become/pay as a sponsor, which complements informational content about sponsorship levels.

evaluations.evidence: use a WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes long-form content creation (e.g., blog posts), so WYSIWYG is a complementary capability rather than exposing a missing prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes sponsors posting jobs and sponsors having sponsorship pages/profiles, enabling the linkage.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes the ability for sponsors to post jobs, so informational guidance is complemented by the underlying capability.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing the job board, providing the complementary read capability for posted jobs.

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes posting jobs, so there is a complementary capability to create content for the job board.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location, so that I can populate the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Assigning rooms/time slots presumes time slots and sessions exist to schedule; backlog includes accepting sessions but lacks an explicit story to create/manage time slots and to place specific sessions into those slots (beyond room assignment).

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a schedule presumes the schedule can be created/populated end-to-end; backlog has partial admin actions (room assignment, session acceptance) but lacks explicit scheduling of sessions into time slots and management of time slots.

evaluations.evidence: see the final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes submitting sessions and admin acceptance/approval actions, which complements publishing a final approved list.

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission and the concept of acceptance, so bulk approval is complemented by the underlying session objects and acceptance state.

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission, providing the complementary capability for sessions to exist to be accepted.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission and acceptance/approval actions, which provides the evaluation outcome that can trigger notifications.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission, which provides the triggering event for a submission confirmation notification.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission, so there is a complementary capability for a session to exist to be edited.

evaluations.evidence: register to speak ... submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes submitting a session, which complements the intent to register to speak by submitting a session.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session ... get my session evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes admin acceptance/approval and notifications about evaluation, which complements session submission and evaluation.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes becoming a sponsor and sponsor-related pages/visibility, so personalization has complementary sponsor presence.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit coordinators listing basic summit information and anonymous users viewing summit lists/details, supporting this listing.

evaluations.evidence: offered several choices of idividual sponsorship ... second page of registration
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes subsequent payment steps for sponsorship registration, complementing the selection step.

evaluations.evidence: find a link in the menu that links to the registration form
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes a user registration form, so the linked destination exists.

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing/updating profiles, which complements having registered user accounts.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission and publishing approved sessions and schedule views, which together provide session information to find.
